newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire's main opposition sends envoys to Kabila.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's main opposition sends envoys to Kabila.

text.p: Zaire's main opposition group said on Thursday it had sent envoys to talk to rebel leader Laurent Kabila, whose forces have been advancing relentlessly in the east and south of the vast Central African country.

"We have delegates en route to meet Mr Kabila," Adrien Phongo, general-secretary of the radical Union for Democracy and Social Progress (UDPS), told a news conference, adding that informal contacts had already been made.
Phongo said the UDPS and Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL) shared a common aim: the overthrow of ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko.

The UDPS of veteran radical Etienne Tshisekedi, a long-standing Mobutu foe, is doing its utmost to unseat Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo -- who has pushed the military option but backed a regional ceasefire call in Kenya on Wednesday.
Kengo, in Nairobi for regional talks on Zaire's crisis, returned to Kinshasa on Thursday saying the job was still his.
"He said when he arrived at midday that he is still prime minister until further notice," one source close to Kengo said.

Citing a disputed Tuesday vote in Zaire's transitional parliament to sack Kengo, Phongo urged Mobutu to endorse Tshisekedi as Zaire's new prime minister. "Mr Tshisekedi must immediately be reinstated as prime minister," he said.

A national conference elected Tshisekedi prime minister in 1992 but Mobutu sacked him a year later in favour of one of his own appointees. Tshisekedi has never accepted Kengo's appointment in 1994 as a later compromise candidate.

The UDPS, like the Zairean government, subscribes to a U.N. sponsored peace plan but Phongo said direct negotiations between Tshisekedi and Kabila could take place before a ceasefire was declared. The government has held out against this.
"The UDPS is convinced talks with Mr Kabila's AFDL will not only take place in a climate of fraternity and patriotism but will have a positive result for all our people," Phongo said.
Mobutu, who left hospital in Europe on Wednesday, plans to return to Zaire on Friday to seek a political solution to its deepening crisis, according to his son, Mobutu Nzanga.
The rebels, who took up arms in October in a dispute about Zairean nationality for an ethnic Tutsi minority, insist on face-to-face talks with Mobutu before any ceasefire.

Kabila's popularity has increased dramatically as his forces have notched up victory after victory. Residents of Kinshasa's poor districts, Tshisekedi's power base, openly welcome the prospect of his arrival in the capital.
Tshisekedi and his party have advocated negotiations to end the war since last year but Phongo's comments suggest that they are anxious to secure a stake in any settlement to the crisis.
While reaffirming its opposition to Mobutu, the UDPS said he had to resolve the political crisis over Kengo's fate, adding that his signature was needed to name a new prime minister.
"Mr Mobutu must implicate himself in the respect of laws. He does not name a prime minister but he is obliged to endorse the designated candidate," Phongo said. REUTER WW NJP
